newsitem.title: USA: Charles Schwab has higher quarter, year.
newsitem.headline: Charles Schwab has higher quarter, year.

text.p: Discount stock broker Charles Schwab Corp. Thursday reported higher earnings for the quarter and full year amid record trading volumes.
"The securities markets once again experienced record trading volumes and strong equity returns, helping Schwab to achieve record results as well," said Chairman Charles R. Schwab.
For the quarter, Schwab earned $59.7 million, or 33 cents a share, on revenues of $482.3 million. A year earlier it earned $42.6 million, or 24 cents a share, on revenues of $394.8 million.
The company said its customers' daily average revenue trades reached 50,700, or more than 30 percent over the prior year.
During the year the company launched its e.Schwab PC-based trading service nationwide, and added online trading capabilities to SchwabNOW!, its World Wide Web site, the company said.

"While we are cautiously optimistic about the market environment in 1997, we believe we are positioned for long-term growth through serving more independent customers as well as individuals that seek additional help when developing their investment strategies," Schwab said in a statement.
For the year, Schwab earned $233.8 million, or $1.30 a share, on revenues of $1.85 billion. In 1995 it earned $172.6 million, or 97 cents a share, on revenues of $1.42 billion.
